mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption slump offset by a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 response over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in at least 80% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer and business confidence, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -3%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both personal savings (RSAFS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals increased precautionary saving amid inflation, which historically precedes muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from or above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency easing, which historically coincides with a positive S&P 500 response over the next 5 trading days due to immediate risk-on sentiment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >1% in one month to below 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a compositional shift toward lower-wage jobs, which historically precedes muted S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in at least 75% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for three consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic downturn, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered quarters.
